title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Which statement best describes the context window of a language model?

options.text: Everything the model can see during one single call, up to a limit
Everything the model has learned from all of its earlier conversations
The saved record of every student that the assistant has served
The set of tools that the model is permitted to request at once

items.stem: An agent's fixed prompt and tool descriptions take 2,000 tokens. Every tool result adds 1,000 tokens to the message list, which is resent in full on each call. The run makes 3 model calls (the first has no tool results yet). How many input tokens are billed in total, ignoring the model's output?

A student chats with your assistant on Tuesday and says they are left-handed and need a different saw guard. On Thursday they open a new session and the assistant does not know this. What is the most direct fix in your program?

options.text: Switch to a model with a much larger context window
Save a note after Tuesday and load it at Thursday's start
Tell the model in its prompt to remember every student
Retrieve more pages from the saw manual for each question

items.stem: In one or two sentences, why is retrieving a few relevant chunks of a long manual usually better than putting the whole manual in the context on every call?
Within one agent run, what is the only thing that carries information from one model call to the next?
